# DGE vs ELK layered

Generated by `DGE_ELK=1 npx vitest run test/benchmark/elk-comparison.test.ts`.

Both engines get identical input: DGE measures and fits every label first, then ELK (elkjs, `layered`, orthogonal routing, `INCLUDE_CHILDREN`, DGE's spacing) lays out the same node sizes, group/lane hierarchy with the same paddings, and the same edge-label sizes. Both results are scored with `measureLayoutQuality`. DGE time is the whole `renderDiagramDsl` call (parse, text measurement, layout, routing, labels, export); ELK time is `elk.layout` alone. ELK has no notion of ports, abutting equal-thickness lanes or explicit constraints, so lanes become ordinary compound nodes there.

Hard = node overlaps + group overlaps + foreign nodes in groups + label overflows + edges through nodes + edge-label collisions + shared endpoints (target 0).
